environment.description: Same EKS cluster (v1.28) but the gRPC service is fronted by an AWS ALB Ingress (using gRPC target group protocol version) with an associated AWS WAFv2 WebACL. The WebACL attaches the AWS managed rule group `AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet` in BLOCK mode with a custom rule that inspects the request body (gRPC payload) for repeated requests with high-entropy base64 payloads exceeding a rate threshold. Additionally, a WAFv2 rate-based rule limits any single source IP to 100 requests per 5-minute window on the `/token_service.TokenValidationService/ValidateToken` URI path. A padding oracle attack requires approximately 256 * (N_blocks * 16) requests (typically 4000-16000+ sequential probes with byte-level mutations). The rate-based rule (100 req/5min) makes it computationally infeasible to complete the oracle within any practical timeframe, as the attack requires observing responses to each probe sequentially before sending the next. The ALB also terminates TLS (ACM cert) so the gRPC channel uses ALPN h2, and the WAF can inspect the full request including serialized protobuf body bytes.

config.ingress: AWS ALB with gRPC target group (protocolVersion: gRPC)
config.network_policy: deny-all ingress except from ALB security group
